chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no wudu (ablution) due to vomiting.

key_terms.قَالَ: he said, marking the transmission of the hadith text
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), the ritual state and act of purification for worship

ai.seo_question: Does vomiting invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that vomiting does not make wudu (ablution) obligatory. It is relevant to questions of ritual purity and the rulings connected to acts of worship, especially salat (prayer).
